Launches the earlier mentioned functionality to steal Google Chrome passwords.
For each identified session, it will access the Windows Explorer shell and duplicate its privileges or security token.
Additionally, the malware checks for presence of tcpview.exe and will not proceed if one is present.

In November 2024, Microsoft Incident Response researchers uncovered a novel remote access trojan (RAT) we named StilachiRAT that demonstrates sophisticated techniques to evade detection, persist in the target environment, and exfiltrate sensitive data.

Analysis of the StilachiRAT’s WWStartupCtrl64.dll module that contains the RAT capabilities revealed the use of various methods to steal information from the target system, such as credentials stored in the browser, digital wallet information, data stored in the clipboard, as well as system information.
Microsoft has not yet attributed StilachiRAT to a specific threat actor or geolocation.
StilachiRAT gathers extensive system information, including OS details, device identifiers, BIOS serial numbers, and camera presence.
StilachiRAT targets a list of specific cryptocurrency wallet extensions for the Google Chrome browser.
StilachiRAT can be launched both as a Windows service or a standalone component.
StilachiRAT monitors RDP sessions by capturing foreground window information and duplicating security tokens to impersonate users.
StilachiRAT collects a variety of user data, including software installation records and active applications.
StilachiRAT has a functionality that is responsible for monitoring clipboard data.
StilachiRAT displays anti-forensic behavior by clearing event logs and checking certain system conditions to evade detection.
StilachiRAT can launch various commands received from the C2 server.

It accesses the settings in the following registry key and validates if any of the extensions are installed:
\SOFTWARE\Google\Chrome\PreferenceMACs\Default\extensions.settings
 However, since the key is encrypted when Chrome is first installed, it uses Windows APIs that rely on current user’s context to decrypt the master key.
Additionally, Windows API calls are obfuscated in multiple ways and a custom algorithm is used to encode many text strings and values.
